Oneliner

Flying around the VESPA debris to precisely reconstruct its shape and dynamics in preparation of its capture for removal.
Description

To rendezvous with and image a European space debris at high resolution.

The ESA funded e.Inspector mission currently in phase B, aims at flying around the VESPA debris to precisely reconstruct its shape and dynamics in preparation of its capture for removal.

The consortium, led by PoliMi, is sizing a 12U CubeSat, equipped with COTS VIS and IR imagers, for multispectral measurements exploitation to enhance performances in relative navigation and target inspection. A dedicated IP-based GNC SW is being developed to manage the whole relative operations, from far to close. A specific processing HW architecture was designed and PIL tests are foreseen to start in short. HIL tests will follow in the GNC PoliMi dark room to verify and confirm the whole HW\SW chain from cameras to relative state reconstruction before entering the next project phase.

To be flexible with respect to launcher release and target debris location at launch, e.Inspector is equipped with qualified electric propulsion currently undergoing endurance tests.
